title: Add cost-model schema package v1 (versioned inputs/outputs + docs + serialization tests)
author: Ethan Park
description:
Motivation: Console, Optimize, telemetry attribution, and billing hooks currently compute “cost” with subtly different definitions (prefill vs decode splits, cache hit accounting, batching efficiency, overhead allocation). This PR introduces a single versioned schema package for Cost Model v1 so downstream callers and producers can converge on the same canonical inputs/outputs, with docs and conformance/serialization tests.

Scope (v1):
- Add a new versioned schema package: //packages/cost-model/schema/v1
- Define canonical request-level inputs (what we can know at request time) vs observed inputs (what runtime/telemetry provides post-hoc) and the canonical cost outputs used by Console/Optimize/finance.
- Provide stable field semantics and naming (aligned with cost breakdown taxonomy work), including “unknown/unavailable” handling.
- Add JSON serialization + round-trip tests and golden fixtures to prevent accidental wire-format drift.

Non-goals:
- Not implementing the Cost Model API service in this PR (handled in ENG-4821/PR-28457).
- Not replacing billing/RevRec; this package defines primitives that billing hooks can consume.

Versioning policy:
- v1 is additive-only for minor releases; any rename/removal requires new major schema version.
- Consumers must ignore unknown fields; producers must not change semantics of existing fields.
- Fields are tagged with stability notes and explicit unit/precision expectations.

Notes for reviewers:
- The schema is designed to support both synchronous request-path estimation and async aggregation. Some fields are marked “required for estimate” vs “required for reconciliation” (telemetry-backed).
- All currency is expressed in USD micros to avoid float ambiguity.
- Token counts are expressed as integers and split by stage (prefill/decode) with optional cached-token attribution.

Follow-ups:
- Wire runtime-exported KV cache metrics into ObservedInputs (ENG-4828).
- Ensure model catalog exposes stable quantization profile identifiers referenced by this schema (ENG-4829).

Docs:
- Schema docs live alongside types and are intended to be source-of-truth for Console/Optimize field semantics until Confluence pages are finalized.

Risk:
- Low runtime risk (types-only). Main risk is accidental churn; mitigated via golden serialization tests and CI checks.
commits: cost-model/schema/v1: introduce core types and enums
docs: add field-level semantics + examples for Console/Optimize
tests: add json round-trip + golden fixtures for deterministic serialization
chore: add lint rules to forbid unversioned schema imports
implementation_notes:
Key schema concepts added in v1: (1) CostModelVersion: explicit version string required on all payloads. (2) DeploymentContext: hosted/dedicated/private + region + hardware_sku + capacity_tier. (3) ModelContext: model_id + model_version + quantization_profile_id + tokenizer_id. (4) RequestUsage: prompt_tokens/complete_tokens with required stage split (prefill_tokens, decode_tokens) and optional cached_token attribution. (5) RuntimeEfficiency: batch_size_effective, queue_time_ms, kv_cache_hit_rate (optional in v1; required once runtime instrumentation lands). (6) CostBreakdown: request_attributable vs overhead_allocated, each split by compute/memory/egress/other; overhead explicitly marked as policy-driven and time-windowed. (7) Confidence: optional confidence interval for estimate-only outputs to support Optimize “what-if” flows; defaults to unknown for observed/reconciled outputs.

The package intentionally avoids embedding product-specific concepts (Console chart buckets, Optimize recommendation IDs). Consumers should map from product concepts into these canonical fields.
review_conversation: Logan Wright: Can we clarify which fields are telemetry-backed vs caller-provided? Right now it reads like everything is required. Also, please call out the expected source of truth for token counts (metering vs runtime).

Ethan Park: Updated docs to tag each field with Source: caller | runtime | metering | finance-policy. Token counts: metering is canonical for billing/reporting; runtime is used for stage split when available (and must reconcile to metering totals within tolerance).
Chloe Martin: Console needs a stable, bounded breakdown for UI tables. Can we guarantee the set of breakdown keys is finite? Also would prefer enum values to match Console naming (prefill/decode).

Ethan Park: Added explicit enum for stages (PREFILL/DECODE) and constrained breakdown categories to a fixed taxonomy. Also documented that per-request breakdown returns a bounded list (no arbitrary tag explosion) and that any additional segmentation happens via aggregation endpoints in the service layer.
Aditya Rao: For Optimize, we need to represent uncertainty for what-if estimates, but it can’t leak into “observed” cost. Can we keep confidence fields optional and clearly scoped?
Ethan Park: Done. Confidence is only valid when output.kind == ESTIMATE (not OBSERVED/RECONCILED). Added validation enforcing that.
Allison Grant: Please align errors/validation wording with internal API standards. Also add a note about ignoring unknown fields for forward compatibility.
Ethan Park: Added compatibility notes and validation guidance; also included a short section in schema/README about forward/backward compatibility expectations.
Sofia Ivanova: batch_size_effective needs a definition (mean over decode? per scheduling window?). Otherwise runtime can’t implement consistently.

Ethan Park: Added precise definition: effective_batch_size is the average concurrent sequences during decode, weighted by decode tokens, over the request lifetime. Also added a placeholder for a future field to capture scheduling window granularity (v2 candidate).
Nadia Rahman: One nit: currency micros should be int64, not number in TS to avoid precision issues. Also ensure JSON uses string encoding if needed.
Ethan Park: In TS we represent micros as string to avoid precision loss; docs updated and golden fixtures now encode micros as strings. Validation enforces digits-only strings.
Elliot Price: Docs are good but please add one end-to-end example payload for Console and one for Optimize so teams don’t guess.
Ethan Park: Added two examples under src/examples with commentary and referenced them from README.
Final review: All requested changes addressed. Approved.
release_notes: Internal-only: Introduces versioned Cost Model schema package v1 for use by Cost Model API service, Console cost breakdown, Optimize ROI modeling, telemetry attribution, and billing hooks. No customer-facing changes in this PR.
notes_for_migration: Consumers should import from packages/cost-model/schema/v1 and include cost_model_version on all payloads. Do not import from the unversioned packages/cost-model/schema root except for shared tooling. Unknown fields must be ignored to allow forward-compat evolution. Currency micros are strings in JSON; do not parse into JS number.
